source.author: verg
source.text: Ast ubi digressum Siculae te admoverit orae ventus, et angusti rarescent claustra Pelori, laeva tibi tellus et longo laeva petantur aequora circuitu: dextrum fuge litus et undas.
source.text_original: 'Ast ubi digressum Siculae te admoverit orae / ventus, et angusti rarescent claustra Pelori, / laeva tibi tellus et longo laeva petantur / aequora circuitu: dextrum fuge litus et undas.
source.text_english: But when the wind has brought you, after your departure, near the Sicilian shore, and the barriers of Pelorus grow sparse at the narrow straits, let the land on your left and the seas on your left be sought by a long circuit: shun the right-hand coast and the waves.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: aequore Trinacrio refugique a parte Pelori stat rupes horrenda fretis: quot in aethera surgit molibus, infernas totidem demissa sub undas.
reuse.text_original: aequore Trinacrio refugique a parte Pelori / stat rupes horrenda fretis: quot in aethera surgit / molibus, infernas totidem demissa sub undas.
reuse.text_english: On the Trinacrian sea and on the side of retreating Pelorus there stands a terrifying rock amid the straits: as many masses as it rises into the air, so many it plunges down beneath the lower waves.
